title: Sheinbaum Says the 152 Hospital Projects Planned for the Six-Year Term Advance, with an Investment of 181 Billion Pesos
author: Alonso Urrutia and Lilian Hernández
content:
_This article by Alonso Urrutia and Lilian Hernández originally appeared in
the[July 21, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/21/politica/avanzan-
los-152-proyectos-hospitalarios-proyectados-para-el-sexenio-con-una-inversion-
de-181-mil-mdp-sheinbaum), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**With an investment of 181 billion pesos over the course of this six-year
term, the federal government will carry out 152 hospital projects, of which 50
will be new hospitals, 47 expansions, and 55 replacements or improvements,
President Claudia Sheinbaum stated, which significantly surpasses construction
during the neoliberal period.**

During the presidential press conference, the Undersecretary of Health,
Eduardo Clark, detailed that with these projects the census beds of the public
health sector will go from 96,966 to 106,105, which represents one of the most
important advances in recent years.

Clark explained that in the first 22 months of this six-year term, 39 projects
have already been completed, which entails 1,474 new census beds. He detailed
that of these 39 projects, seven correspond to the IMSS, 17 to IMSS Bienestar,
and twelve to the ISSSTE.

In turn, the director of the ISSSTE, Martí Batres, stated that to date this
institution aims for the construction, modernization, or rehabilitation of 20
hospital units, four of which are already completed. Among the ISSSTE's main
projects, he highlighted the General Zone Hospital in Chetumal, the hospital
clinic in Chilpancingo, the Vasco de Quiroga Hospital in Morelia, and the new
clinic in San Quintín, in Baja California.

For his part, the director of the IMSS, Zoe Robledo, highlighted that this
institution plans to build 47 hospitals during this six-year term, of which
seven are already operating and 21 are already under construction. Among them
he highlighted the General Hospitals of Guanajuato, Navojoa, Tula, Ensenada,
Ticul, San Quintín, Santa Catarina, Zitácuaro, and Guadalupe, among others.

In turn, the director of IMSS Bienestar, Alejandro Svarch, reported that this
institution plans to invest 46 billion pesos, including 19 projects in a
network of 19 new hospitals in Tijuana, Tlapa, Jiutepec, Tuxtepec, and Ixtlán
de Juárez.

Further on, Sheinbaum reported that between 1943 and 1982, before the
neoliberal period, 29,500 beds were created in Mexico. However, in this latter
period, over 36 years, only 4,300 beds were added. She emphasized that from
December 2018 to September 2030, 13,300 new census beds are expected to be
added.
